messages:

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Subject: On-prem tenant surface routing constraints & control/data confirmation

Matt / Acme network team —

Thanks for the Friday sync. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the outstanding constraints and ask for confirmation on the approach we're about to move forward with for the private (on-prem) tenant deployment that will host Acme workloads. High level ask: confirm a minimal, auditable control plane path and a safe data plane routing pattern that meets your egress/ingress policy.

Key constraints we captured:
- No inbound routes into tenant network from internet (only specific reverse-proxied endpoints allowed)
- No BGP peering allowed from customer edge to Redwood for this engagement (Acme policy)
- Outbound egress must be allow-listed to a short set of IPs (control plane, telemetry, and package fetch endpoints)
- Mutual TLS required for control-plane API; telemetry must flow via an approved proxy
- Management plane (kube/ops) access via jump-host in Acme mgmt VLAN only; no direct port ranges allowed to tenant nodes

Proposed Redwood patterns (for discussion):
1) Control plane: outbound-only TLS connections from control-plane agents to Redwood control endpoints. We will provide a fixed set of IPs and FQDNs for allowlisting. No inbound NAT required.
2) Data plane: tenant workloads stay on Acme fabric; Redwood runtime is packaged as on-prem gateways that accept only local traffic and use SNAT for egress to approved endpoints.
3) Telemetry/metrics: route over Acme egress proxy (recommended) or push to customer-approved S3 via secure token exchange.

Deliverables requested from Acme to finalize design:
- Confirm whether SNAT is acceptable for tenant egress (we can provide per-tenant NAT pools).
- Confirm list of IP ranges you can allowlist for control-plane + build time estimate for security review.
- Any firewall ACL snippets or example ACL rules you require for the control/telemetry flows.

Attachments: redwood_onprem_ref_diagram_v1.pdf (reference diagram), acme_request_sheet.xlsx (short inventory).

Target next steps: if we get the confirmation today, Vanessa + Jonas will produce redwood_onprem_ref_diagram_v2 with port-level annotations and a canary schedule.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifications from Acme networking/security: we cannot accept BGP peering as noted. SNAT is acceptable but we need per-tenant source IPs so downstream logging can attribute traffic.

Control plane: we will allow outbound TLS to a whitelist of IPs/ports. We also require mTLS client certs for the agents.
Telemetry: must go via our egress proxy host (proxy.acme.corp:3128). No direct outbound to unknown S3 endpoints.

Attached is a quick snippet of the edge ACLs we typically apply (ports and allowed destinations). Also included is a small topology sketch showing management VLAN separation.

Attachments: acme_infra_snippet.png, acme_edge_acl.txt

If you can update the diagram with per-tenant SNAT ranges and control-plane FQDNs/IPs, we can start the security review next week.

Matt

Subject: Re: On-prem tenant surface routing constraints & control/data confirmation

Folks —

Thanks Matt for the quick feedback. Based on Acme constraints, here's what I recommend and why: 

1) Per-tenant SNAT pools: implement per-tenant NAT addresses at Acme edge. Redwood runtime will be configured to use the assigned SNAT range per tenant so downstream systems see a consistent source. This meets logging/attribution needs.

2) Control plane: outbound-only mTLS from our control agents to control.redwood.example (we will provide cert provisioning steps). We'll publish a short list of Egress IPs (three /32s) and a stable DNS name for failover. Acme team to allow TLS to these endpoints.

3) Telemetry: route to Acme proxy. Redwood agents will send metrics to localhost:9100 which are then forwarded by the proxy; we will also support proxy auth with TLS client certs or token header as required.

4) No inbound access: agree — no inbound port openings are necessary. For any debug sessions, we recommend a temporary jump-host session using Acme IAM-managed bastion (we will coordinate SRE runbook).

Config snippet (example for control agent outbound):

# control-agent.yaml (excerpt)
control: 
  endpoint: https://control.redwood.example:8443
  mTLS: true
  client_cert: /etc/redwood/certs/client.pem
  ca_bundle: /etc/redwood/certs/ca.pem
  egress_via: proxy.acme.corp:3128    # optional, if required by Acme

Caveats: if Acme requires deep packet inspection that breaks TLS, we will need an exception for the control API connections or a proxy that terminates TLS with mutual auth from both sides (we should avoid MITM on control plane).

I'll update the reference diagram with port annotations and the SNAT mapping for per-tenant pools and send v2 for review.

Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Product Engineer, Deployment Platforms
Redwood Inference
